mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent earnings reductions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a strong supply-side recovery, which typically boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) are increasing, the combination signals a tight labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of low UNRATE and increasing PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strong demand for housing, which typically boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent sector performance.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a rapid tightening phase, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening phases.
